proof.criterion: A2 (R1). Negative control: one session posts 6 times with no human event. Its last answer carries "Stop posting".
proof.surface: The same branch `dispatch` command against the server built from this change on port 8777.
proof.command: bash /tmp/infra-184/prove.sh (section A2): six `dispatch message --issue PRF-2` runs, all with DISPATCH_SESSION_ID=a2-solo, on a fresh issue with no human event.
proof.observed: The sixth run printed `Posted. You've sent 6 messages on PRF-2 with no human response. Stop posting here until a human replies.` and recorded session_writes_since_human = 6: a session's own cadence is still counted and still told.

proof.criterion: A3 (R2). A claim on an issue that carries `legion`, one that carries `Legion`, and one whose parent carries it, none of them name `issue-update`; nor does releasing a claim on them. Negative control: a claim and a release on an issue with no such label on it or above it still say to move the status.
proof.surface: The same branch `dispatch` command against the server built from this change on port 8777, on four issues created through the command itself: PRF-3 (label `legion`), PRF-4 (label `Legion`), PRF-6 (no label, parent PRF-5 labelled `legion`), PRF-7 (label `infra`).
proof.command: bash /tmp/infra-184/prove.sh (section A3): `dispatch claim --issue <KEY>` then `dispatch claim --issue <KEY> --release` for each of the four, each run's stdout asserted both ways — it must not match `issue-update`, and it must match the new sentence naming Legion as the mover, so the check cannot pass on empty output.
proof.observed: All three Legion-owned issues answered, on both routes, `… Legion's daemon moves this issue's status on an issue it runs, so leave it alone — a status written here is undone.` and named `issue-update` nowhere. 14 assertions, 0 failures.
proof.negativeControl: PRF-7, with no `legion` label on it or above it, still answered `… a claim moves nothing, so move it to in_progress with dispatch issue-update when you start, and release the claim when you stop.` on the claim and `… — move it yourself if that is no longer where the work is.` on the release, byte for byte today's text. Separately, the pod's installed pre-change `dispatch` run against the same server on the same labelled issue PRF-3 still said `move it to in_progress with dispatch issue-update`, so the server field alone does not carry the fix: both halves are needed.

proof.criterion: A4 (R3). `dispatch doc-edit --issue <KEY> --ops-json-file -` with no artifact edits the spec, and reaches the same document as `--artifact spec`. Negative control: on an issue that also carries an uploaded plan.md, `--artifact plan.md` still edits that document and leaves the spec alone.
proof.surface: The same branch `dispatch` command against the server built from this change on port 8777, on PRF-8: an issue created with a spec and carrying an uploaded plan.md.
proof.command: bash /tmp/infra-184/prove.sh (section A4): `dispatch doc-edit --issue PRF-8 --ops-json-file -` with no `--artifact`, then `dispatch doc-read --issue PRF-8 --artifact spec`, then a second edit with `--artifact spec`, then `dispatch doc-edit --issue PRF-8 --artifact plan.md --ops-json-file -`, then `dispatch doc-read --issue PRF-8`.
proof.observed: The no-artifact edit applied and minted spec version 2; `--artifact spec` read the new text back; the following `--artifact spec` edit minted version 3, so both reached one artifact. This is the command `skills/legion-architect/SKILL.md:114` shows, which was refused before.
proof.negativeControl: `--artifact plan.md` minted plan.md version 2 while the spec stayed at version 3 with its own text; `--project PRF` with no artifact is still refused, `Exactly one of issue and project is required; with project, artifact names the document.`; and the pod's installed pre-change `dispatch`, run against the same server with the same arguments, still refused with `Exactly one of issue and project is required; artifact or ref must name the document.`

trickyParts: The new field must not go on `model.Issue`: it is embedded in `model.IssueEventPayload`, the payload of every `issue.*` event, so a read-resolved value there would leak into events. It rides a response wrapper that embeds `model.Issue`, keeping the JSON flat, which is what the dashboard's release call needs (it merges the body straight into its issue cache) and what every Go test that decodes the body needs.

Moving the non-session early return above the count query broke `TestDocumentEditAdviceKeepsCountWhenIssueAdviceFails`, which forced a query failure through a human's document edit: a human now runs no advice query, so there was nothing left to fail. The test drives the same failure as a session, which is the only actor that reaches those queries. The whole `internal/dispatch/api` package was run to find it; the `-run WriteAdvice` filter did not match that test's name.

`documentOwnerValidation`'s `alwaysRequireArtifact` branch stays as it is: `dispatch_suggest` uses it directly and still requires an artifact, because its execute path reads the argument as required — relaxing it would turn a clear refusal into a thrown error.
deviations: The spec's Acceptance says each criterion is proven against a server `bun run dispatch:local` starts. The plan departed to `packages/dispatch/e2e/run-server.sh`, the same Go server built from the same tree without the single-page-application build and the Playwright listener set that no criterion reads; this round followed the plan.

The plan's Task 0b calls for a rootless Postgres with `initdb --locale=C`. The Go suite's `TestIssueRanksStayOrderedPastLowercaseDigitsAndProductionShapedMoves` refuses to run on a byte-order database (it says so itself, rank_test.go:317), so a second cluster was initialised with `--locale-provider=icu --icu-locale=en-US` and the suite was run against that. Nothing in the product changed for it.
openQuestions: A fourth wrong text, outside this issue's three requirements, is still live and was seen on every run above: after a write to an issue still in triage the client appends "<KEY> is still in triage — nobody can see its development status. See the `dispatch` skill, 'Issue status is yours to move'." (packages/envoy-client/src/dispatch-execute.ts:267-277). On an issue Legion runs that advice is wrong in exactly the way R2 fixes, and the fix is not free: write advice rides every message, comment and ask, so answering it would put the parent walk on that hot path. Reported to the architect; the plan names it too (departure 2).
discoveredComplexity: The claim and release results are not the only place the status instruction lives: `dispatch_claim`'s own description carries it too, and that text has no issue in hand. It could not be made conditional, so it now says the result names who moves the status.

`dispatch doc-edit`'s reference hint (`innerRefProblem`) asserted that naming an issue alone would be refused for doc-edit. R3 makes that false, so the hint was reworded; the spec's Design had said the passage stayed true (the plan recorded the departure).
